title: No AVX-512 copy of simd::dot: measured, nothing to gain on Zen 4
body: The todo's first piece, measured before switching (simd::tests::timing, ignored, kept): dot_kernel made generic over its accumulator count (dot_lanes<T, L>; dot_kernel stays L = 16, so every caller's bits are unchanged) and timed per copy on this Zen 4. GFLOP/s, f32 at 4 Ki (in cache): baseline 40, AVX2 58, AVX-512 with 16 accumulators 56, with 64 46; f64: 10 / 21 / 21 / 21 (32 accumulators); at 1 Mi (from memory) every copy is within 35-37 (f32) and 17-18 (f64). Zen 4 runs 512-bit floating-point arithmetic as two 256-bit halves, and out of cache memory bandwidth bounds it, so an AVX-512 copy adds code and a second summation order for no speed: dot and sum keep their AVX2 dispatch, as do the loops that inline dot_kernel. The rasterizer is different (its integer and conversion work gains: 10.5x against 8.5x with AVX2). Reopen on a CPU with full-width AVX-512 units: the timing test prints the comparison. The second piece is done: fill_row takes its square roots in a pass over 64-pixel blocks through the lanes' sqrt, so a no-std build uses each target's square-root instruction (16 sqrtps per block on x86-64 without std, no libm calls), and the std build got faster too (4.2x / 8.5x / 10.5x a plain loop, from 3.5 / 6.7 / 9.0), the same bytes.
